Chapter 9: Sustaining Momentum—Habits, Rituals, and the Long Game
When you think about outrageous success, it’s easy to imagine a single, life-changing moment. But the truth? Success is built little by little, through steady effort over time. That momentum you need doesn’t just show up—it’s created by the habits and rituals you practice every day, even on those mornings when your motivation is nowhere to be found.
Think of habits as the rails a train runs on. They give you direction and structure, helping you stay on track, no matter what comes your way. Now, rituals are a bit different. They add intention and meaning to your day, turning even the simplest actions into powerful reminders of why you started in the first place.
Picture an athlete gearing up for a big season. Every morning, they start with a simple ritual—maybe visualizing their goals, checking their training plan, and pausing for a moment of gratitude. It sounds small, but this daily practice sets the tone and keeps their purpose front and center.
If you’re wondering how to keep your own momentum going, here are a few strategies you might want to try:
First, set up morning and evening routines. Think of these as bookends for your day—habits that support what you want to achieve.
Next, track your progress in a way you can actually see. Maybe it’s a chart on your wall, a journal, or an app. Watching your progress stack up is more motivating than you’d expect.
Make a habit of reviewing and adjusting. Take a little time each week to ask yourself what’s working, and what needs a tweak.
And don’t just wait for the big wins to celebrate. Consistency is worth recognizing, too—showing up every day, even when it’s tough, is a win all on its own.
Here’s something to really pay attention to: keeping momentum takes patience. Progress is almost never a straight line. Some weeks, you’ll leap forward. Other times, it might feel like you’re standing still. The most important thing is to trust the process and keep moving, even if you can’t see results right away.
Over time, those small, steady actions start to add up—and before you know it, they become something extraordinary. By focusing on your habits and rituals, you’ll give yourself the best shot at maintaining momentum and sticking with your biggest, boldest goals.
